description.value:
The Sky turns without you. One of thirteen skies is up each day, its aspect is Quiet, Benefic, Retrograde, Malefic or Exalted, rolled at the weights in §8.2. Almost nobody can tell which.

During your daily preparations, spend 10 minutes observing the sky. (Indoors, underground or under cloud there is no sky to observe, and your chart is not a substitute — see Clouded Sky.) You gain three things:

  1. Certainty. You learn today’s sign and its aspect exactly. No check, no DC, no ambiguity.
  2. The Forecast. You learn the sign and aspect of the next three days. The sky is fixed before anyone looks at it, so this answer does not change if you ask again.
  3. Augury of the Day. You add the ascendant sign’s Augury to your repertoire until your next daily preparations. On a Starless sky you gain no Augury of the Day — but nothing is written, so you may roll your Portent twice and keep either result.

Forewarned. You may spend a further 10 minutes briefing up to five allies. You and each ally who listens reduce the day’s negative aspect by one step for the rest of the day: Malefic → Retrograde, Retrograde → no effect. Positive aspects are unchanged.

Clouded Sky. If you cannot complete a Night Vigil you learn nothing, gain no Augury of the Day, get no forecast, and cannot use Forewarned. The GM marks a clouded night on the Sky tracker.

Runs by itself when you Rest for the Night: the card is whispered to you, with Forewarned as a button on it.
